# Results — Study 305 (Gold-Oil-Ratio) on real daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The gold/oil ratio used as a
binary **risk-on/risk-off market-timing switch** for SPY: hold SPY when the standardised
60-day deviation of the log gold/oil ratio is at or below +1 (risk-on); sit in cash (the
^IRX T-bill rate) when it exceeds +1 (gold expensive vs oil → risk-off). Signal known at the
close of *t*, position held on *t+1* (one execution lag). Raced — on an **excess-of-cash**
basis — against buy-and-hold SPY and against a **random-timing control** with the identical
cash fraction. As-of **2026-06-19**; match the per-series fingerprint to confirm the tape.*

## Data stamp

| Series | Ticker | Window | Days | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|--:|---|
| Gold | GLD | 2006-04-10 → 2026-05-29 | 5,066 | `5ba35824fbb5` |
| Oil | USO | 2006-04-10 → 2026-05-29 | 5,066 | `321b0cac16ee` |
| Equity | SPY | 2006-04-10 → 2026-05-29 | 5,066 | `80795ab4730b` |
| Cash | ^IRX | (13-week T-bill, daily) | 5,066 | — |

The partial month after 2026-05-29 is dropped before the stats. The common-history start
(2006-04-10) is the inception of the USO oil ETF.

## The headline — canonical switch (lookback 60, enter z > +1, 5 bps/switch, net)

| Book | ann. return | excess-of-cash Sharpe | max drawdown | % days long | HAC *t* (excess ≠ 0) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Gold/oil switch** | **+8.88%** | **+0.594** | **−29.0%** | 71.5% | +2.92 |
| Buy-and-hold SPY | +11.19% | +0.561 | −55.2% | 100.0% | +2.93 |
| Random-timing control | +1.36% | +0.065 | −53.1% | 71.5% | +0.32 |

- The switch's **excess-of-cash Sharpe (0.594)** is a hair above buy-and-hold's (0.561), and
  it roughly **halves the worst drawdown** (−29% vs −55%) by sitting out the 2008 crash.
- But it gives up **−2.3%/yr of return** (8.88% vs 11.19%) to do it, and the head-to-head
  test says the difference is **not** real:

| Head-to-head (net excess-of-cash daily return) | HAC *t* | 95% block-bootstrap CI (bps/day) |
|---|--:|---|
| Switch − Buy-and-hold | **−1.20** | [−3.18, +0.87] |
| Switch − Random-timing | **+2.30** | [+0.32, +5.08] |

The switch **never beats buy-and-hold** — and it edges the random-timing control at this one
seed (t = +2.30), but that result is **fragile**: averaged over 20 random-control seeds the
*t* is **+1.87**, i.e. *below* the |*t*| ≥ 2 bar. So the gold/oil ratio carries *some*
defensive regime information, but not enough to certify a real timing edge.

## Robustness — the timing claim fails at every setting

The folklore claim is that the ratio *times equities* — i.e. beats buy-and-hold. Across a
4 × 3 grid of (lookback, threshold) the switch's *t* versus buy-and-hold is **negative in all
twelve cells**; the *t* versus random timing clears 2 only at the longer lookbacks:

| lookback | z > +1.0 | z > +1.5 | z > +2.0 |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 40  | *t*_bh −1.76 / *t*_rand +1.66 | −1.98 / +0.50 | −1.40 / −0.46 |
| 60  | **−1.20 / +2.30** | −0.86 / +1.62 | −1.68 / +0.03 |
| 120 | −1.40 / +3.07 | −0.07 / +2.34 | −0.07 / +1.19 |
| 200 | −1.78 / +3.27 | −1.02 / +1.92 | −0.74 / +0.14 |

Buy-and-hold's excess Sharpe is +0.56 throughout; the switch tops it only marginally and only
in the cells where it happens to dodge a drawdown.

## The edge is one regime, not a durable signal

Splitting at 2015 shows the entire defensive benefit is a **pre-2015 artefact** — the 2008
GFC crash, when gold spiked and oil collapsed so the ratio screamed "risk-off" right before
the worst of the equity drawdown:

| Sub-period | switch ann. | B&H ann. | *t* vs B&H | *t* vs random | switch maxDD | B&H maxDD |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Pre-2015  | +10.4% | +7.6%  | +0.28 | +1.70 | −29% | −55% |
| Post-2015 | +8.0%  | +14.0% | −1.93 | +0.30 | −29% | −34% |

Post-2015 the switch *loses* to buy-and-hold and its edge over random timing vanishes
(*t* = +0.30). The signal does not survive out of the crisis that birthed it.

## Could you trade it? — the cost sweep

| round-trip cost | switch ann. | switch excess Sharpe | *t* vs B&H |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 0 bps (gross) | +9.65% | +0.649 | −0.93 |
| 2 bps | +9.34% | +0.627 | −1.04 |
| 5 bps | +8.88% | +0.594 | −1.20 |
| 10 bps | +8.10% | +0.539 | −1.46 |
| 20 bps | +6.58% | +0.429 | −1.99 |

286 switches over 20 years (~14/yr) — costs are modest, but they don't matter: even gross,
the switch trails buy-and-hold's return and ties its Sharpe. There is no cost at which a
return-timing edge appears, because there is no return-timing edge to begin with.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is a faithful detector

On a deterministic synthetic tape the same engine recovers a switch edge **only when a
forward link from the lagged ratio to equity returns is planted** (`pred_r < 0`,
folklore-consistent: high ratio precedes lower returns); on the null (`pred_r = 0`) it cannot:

| Planted `pred_r` | switch excess Sharpe | B&H excess Sharpe | *t* vs B&H | signal? |
|---|--:|--:|--:|:--:|
| 0.00 (null) | −0.16 | −0.06 | −0.59 | no |
| −0.005 | +4.76 | +1.10 | +11.35 | yes |
| −0.01 | +7.46 | +1.64 | +12.22 | yes |

The engine banks a planted timing signal cleanly and finds nothing on the null — so the
real-tape "no" is a statement about the market, not a broken detector.

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** The claim is that the ratio *times equities* (beats buy-and-hold); that
  is rejected in all twelve robustness cells (*t* vs B&H negative everywhere). The only real
  thing is a defensive risk-cut versus random timing, and even that is fragile — *t* = +2.30
  at the canonical seed but **+1.87 averaged over 20 seeds**, below the bar, and it is a
  pre-2015 (GFC) artefact that dies post-2015 (*t* vs random +0.30).
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The switch trails buy-and-hold by ~2.3%/yr for a statistically
  tied Sharpe; no cost level reveals an edge because there is none over the passive default.
  You pay return to buy a drawdown cut you can get more cheaply with a constant lower weight.
- **Does it time equities like Dr. Copper? — BUSTED.** The gold/oil ratio is a *defensive
  regime gauge* (it halves the crash-era drawdown and beats random timing pre-2015) but not
  an equity *timer*: it loses to simply holding SPY in every parameterisation and every cost.
